name: Solar + Battery Payback in Los Angeles County Under NEM 3.0

mainEntity.name: What is the realistic payback time for a solar + battery system in Los Angeles County after the NEM 3.0 changes?
mainEntity.text: What is the realistic payback time for a solar + battery system in Los Angeles County after the NEM 3.0 changes?

acceptedAnswer.text: NEM 3.0 significantly changed the math for grid-tied solar in Los Angeles County by cutting export credits and shifting value toward self-consumption and load shifting. For an average single-family home, solar-only systems now commonly pay back in roughly 8–11 years, assuming good sun exposure, stable roof, and rising utility rates. Adding a battery generally extends payback to the 10–14 year range because of higher upfront cost, but batteries can unlock extra savings by storing midday solar and discharging during expensive evening time-of-use periods. Your actual payback depends on several local factors: whether you are with LADWP, SCE, or a municipal utility, your current tiered/time-of-use rate structure, and how much of your daytime usage can be shifted. Battery programming is critical; poorly configured batteries can underperform financially. To refine the estimate, gather 12 months of bills, note your rate plan, and request proposals that model NEM 3.0 exports, realistic degradation, and separate scenarios with and without storage. Ask installers to show side‑by‑side payback and internal rate of return, and to run a sensitivity analysis for future rate hikes. Also consider non-financial benefits: backup power for outages, comfort, and protection against future tariff changes, which often justify batteries even when they lengthen the strict payback period.
acceptedAnswer.description: Under California’s NEM 3.0 rules, a typical Los Angeles County home often sees solar-only payback in 8–11 years, while solar plus battery can range 10–14 years. Actual payback depends heavily on your usage pattern, utility (LADWP vs SCE), battery size, and how well your system is programmed for new time-of-use rates.
